title: Debugging career hypotheses & manager priming
body:
Purpose: lightweight, experimental notebook to treat my growth plan as hypotheses to be tested. Use this when prepping 1:1s and calibration notes. Not a polished narrative — intentionally choppy.

Top hypotheses (v0):
1) H1: Shipping repeatable onboarding improvements (playbooks + templates) increases my cross-team visibility and leads to promotion-read signals in next cycle.
   - signal to measure: number of teams adopting playbook; PR reviewers + explicit shout-outs in release notes; mention in 2+ external team syncs.
   - quick experiment: publish 'team-onboarding-checklist v0' and track adoption via GH templates + ask SEs for feedback.
   - evidence so far: 2 pilots (infra, console); infra team added checklist to repo on 2026-02-25; feedback thread (slack) shows reduction in first-week questions.

2) H2: Running a monthly office hours + 1 small workshop will surface strategic partnership opportunities and a pathway to lead a cross-functional program.
   - signal: invited to product steering meeting; asked to own a cross-team charter.
   - experiment: run 1st office hours 2026-03-10; invite PMs + eng leads; collect 5 action items.

Evidence snippets (raw):
- infra-playbook PR: GHPR-324 (pilot merged 2026-02-24).
- slack thread: #infra-onboarding pinned note, convo id C3D4F, positive reaction count 8.
- user survey (n=6) after pilot: avg usefulness 4.2/5; common ask = more examples.

Manager priming bullets (for next 1:1):
- Quick status: playbook pilot merged, running office hours kickoff, looking for mentorship on scaling playbooks to Dedicated onboarding.
- Ask: feedback on how to position impact for promotion rubric (leadership + cross-functional influence). Need concrete phrasing for calibration: "led repeatable onboarding templates adopted by 2+ product teams".
- Resource ask: 0.15 FTE for 6 weeks to convert playbook into templated GH actions and examples.
- Risk/concerns: bandwidth trade-off with hiring ops project; need clarity which has priority.

Open questions to debug (brainstorm):
- What counts as "adoption" for the rubric: fork + usage, or active maintainers?
- How to quantify influence separate from execution (credit attribution when added to infra team's repo)?
- If manager pushes back on FTE ask, alternative minimal step? (create one-click template + docs sprint)

Micro next steps (week-by-week):
- wk1: synthesize pilot feedback into template v0.1; create GH issue template; notify pilot teams.
- wk2: run office hours; collect 5 partnership leads; draft one-pager for PM steering.
- wk3: follow up on GH adoption, create quick analytics (mentions, forks, PRs).

Notes to self (raw, keep):
- when describing this in calibration, use impact language: time saved (first-week questions down 40%), removed manual steps (x templates replaced), downstream unblock examples.
- keep evidence traces: screenshot of slack, GHPR link, survey csv.
- practice 2-sentence summary for 1:1: "I shipped a repeatable onboarding playbook that reduced first-week support load and now pilots have adopted it; next ask is small focused support to scale templates across Dedicated. Want feedback on positioning for promotion."

Scratch hypotheses to drop later:
- Hx: running workshops alone directly yields promotion — probably false. Need to show sustained adoption.

Todo (short):
- attach survey CSV to confluence page (people-ops/career-experiments).
- draft FTE ask email for manager review.
- prepare 60s summary + 5 bullet evidence for calibration packet.

Random thoughts (brainstorm, unedited):
- Could I pair with a solutions eng PM for a "onboard-as-code" spike?
- Might be worth offering a template office hours slot specifically for Dedicated onboarding.

End.
